messages:
devon: Heads up — saw a spike in multi-GPU OOMs on TP=8 smoke tests after yesterday's runtime merge. 2 failures out of 20 runs.

maria: Which test? sequence length / batch / kv cache footprint?

devon: Mostly long-seq (max_seq=2048) with kv cache enabled, batch_size=1 but infer-time temp buffers still large. Profiling shows an extra ~1.2GB per-GPU transient from comm + temp allocs.

aj: I pulled an ncu trace and there's a big cudaMalloc/free hotspot during the forward, looks like kernel workspace allocations per-layer.

ciara: That rings a bell — recent change to kernel selection added a fallback path that allocs a per-op workspace instead of reusing the global workspace. Could be the regression.

maria: Can you paste the ncu summary?

devon: Paste: 
```
==PROF== GPU:0 transient_allocs: 1.18GB peak; cudaMallocAsync hits: 0; cudaMalloc/free pairs: 42
==PROF== NCCL: comm-buffer total per-rank: 512MB (allreduce + reduce-scatter temporary fragmentation)
==PROF== KV cache storage: expected 6.5GB steady, but transient + temp pushes live set > 8GB
```

aj: Interesting — cudaMallocAsync is off, so allocator falls back to cudaMalloc which fragments. We should toggle to cudaMallocAsync + a pooling allocator to avoid those per-kernel mallocs.

ciara: Also NCCL temp buffers scaled with tensor-parallel shard count. For smaller per-device shard sizes, the comm code currently allocs a full buffer instead of a minimal chunk — we can shrink that.

maria: Proposed quick fixes: 1) enable cudaMallocAsync + pool, 2) add a reusable per-device comm pool sized by shard bytes, 3) revert kernel fallback to reuse global workspace when available. Thoughts?

devon: Agree. Priorities: stop repeated malloc/free first (biggest perf/fragmentation hit), then address comm buffer sizing.

aj: I prototyped a small allocator config in runtime conf: 
```
allocator:
  use_cudaMallocAsync: true
  pool_initial_mb: 4096
  pool_growth_mb: 1024
  allow_shrink: true
  shrink_threshold: 0.25
```
This dropped transient mallocs by ~95% in my fork and peak mem by ~1.0GB on 8-GPU job.

ciara: For NCCL, implemented a lazy comm-pool: allocate comm buffers proportional to (shard_bytes * factor) where factor = min(1.0, max_batch_tokens/target_tokens). In practice that kept per-rank comm buffers to ~128MB instead of 512MB for our small-shard config.

maria: Nice. Any kernel changes needed?

aj: A small kernel-selection tweak: prefer fused-kernel variants that accept an externally provisioned workspace pointer to avoid internal temp alloc. We had fallen back to generic kernels that malloc internally. Patch is tiny — pass global_workspace into fused path.

devon: We should be careful with workspace sizing: larger workspace helps fused kernels but costs memory. Suggest heuristic: choose workspace = min( per-layer-recommended, global_pool_remaining * 0.6 ). If insufficient, fall back to streaming-friendly kernel that uses less workspace but maybe slower.

ciara: Also worth enabling a runtime flag to prefer latency SLO vs memory SLO. For latency, keep current fused kernels and larger workspace; for memory-constrained infra, force low-workspace kernels + slightly higher CPU-side batching.

maria: Can someone open a short PR for allocator + comm-pool today? I'll own kernel fallback revert.

aj: I'll push allocator + tests this afternoon — will run our multi-gpu smoke. PR will include an option to run with use_cudaMallocAsync=false for older drivers.

ciara: I'll add a unit to compute comm-buffer target size and a guard to cap at 25% of free device memory.

devon: Great. After PRs, let's run the long-seq stress for 12 hours. If we still see >1% OOMs, we'll instrument a snapshotter to dump live allocations when free<threshold.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: runway/runtime-r1234 queued for canary on gcp-us-west1-tp8 at +10m.

maria: Thanks — please post perf numbers in this thread when available. :thumbsup:

aj: Quick note — for reproducibility, I added a small cli flag: `--alloc-trace` that emits simple summaries instead of full ncu to keep logs small.

devon: Perfect. If the allocator + comm-pool fixes reduce transient by ~1GB, we should be back to stable. I'll follow up with trace if not.

ciara: Filing a short postmortem checklist after fixes: 1) add unit for per-op workspace reuse, 2) add comm-buffer cap, 3) test cudaMallocAsync on CI images, 4) add kernel-selection integration test to ensure no accidental fallback.

maria: Solid plan. Closing loop once canary passes.
